ads_ratio.reason: EDGAR diluted share counts are in ordinary shares while the Nasdaq price is per ADS; per-share figures must be scaled x2 ordinary shares per ADS to be comparable to the ADS price
ads_ratio.source: JD.com Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (filed 2025-04-17), Item 9.A Offering and Listing Details: the company's ADSs, each representing two Class A ordinary shares, have been listed on Nasdaq since May 22, 2014 under the symbol JD; the same ratio is stated on the 20-F cover for the registered ADS class

moat_against: Almost no consumer lock-in: shoppers multi-home across Alibaba, Pinduoduo and Douyin with near-zero switching costs
Food delivery is a bought, anti-moat position: #3 vs Meituan's structural density lead, and it burned the group's FY2025 economics
Structurally thin group economics: net margin 2-3% in good years, modest returns on a huge logistics asset base
Recurring regulatory/political overhang: SAMR fine in H1 2026, repeated subsidy-war intervention, standing China/VIE ADS tail risk
Category concentration: electronics/appliances demand now partly driven by fading government trade-in subsidies (Q2 2026 category revenue -11.8% YoY)
moat_for: Owned logistics network (warehouses, employed couriers, full-time delivery rider fleet) sets the same/next-day standard and is increasingly monetized to third parties
1P supply-chain scale in electronics/appliances: procurement leverage and authenticity trust; JD Retail gross margin expanded 17 straight quarters to a record operating margin in H1 2026
Mix shift to asset-light services (marketplace, marketing/ads, logistics services) raises the group's structural margin ceiling
Fortress liquidity (cash, restricted cash and short-term investments of RMB 235.1B at June 2026 per the Q2 2026 release) plus buybacks fund investment without balance-sheet stress
moat_justification: Owned logistics network and 1P supply-chain scale drive record JD Retail margins, but consumers multi-home with near-zero switching costs, food delivery is a cash-burning #3 position management chose to buy, group margins are structurally thin, and China regulatory overhang is recurring.
name: JD.com, Inc.
one_liner: China's strongest logistics/supply-chain retailer, moat 5/10 — Tier A by numbers on the v5 normalized median base ($4.43/ADS): weighted IRR 20.3%, IV@15% $38.45 vs $26.60 — but that base sits at pre-food-delivery-war FY2024 economics and trough/TTM bases clear less, so size it like a B; the bear case ($30.70) also sits above the current price.
